forecasts.forecast: FOMC holds the federal funds target range at 3.50-3.75% on Jul 29, with no cut.
forecasts.basis: Prediction-market pricing (Polymarket) and futures-implied odds reported at 83-85% for a hold, cited across multiple financial press sources ahead of a non-SEP meeting.
forecasts.outcome: FOMC held 3.50-3.75% on Jul 29 (9-3 vote, historic 3-way hawkish dissent).
forecasts.lesson: Prediction-market/futures-implied odds (83-85% hold) were well-calibrated for this meeting.

forecasts.forecast: Q2 2026 GDP advance estimate (Jul 30, 8:30 ET) prints in a 1.5-3.0% annualized range.
forecasts.basis: No GDPNow/tracking-estimate data was reachable this run (FRED key not configured); range is a wide default band reflecting genuine uncertainty rather than a modeled estimate — treat as low-confidence.
forecasts.outcome: Q2 GDP advance printed +1.5% annualized -- inside the stated 1.5-3.0% range, but exactly at the bottom edge.
forecasts.lesson: The range was wide enough to technically capture the outcome, but a 55-65%-probability band centered well above the eventual print understated downside growth risk; the GDPNow-informed 1.0-2.5% band issued the next morning (2026-07-27-am-2) was better centered.

forecasts.forecast: At least one of the five mega-cap reporters (MSFT, META, AAPL, AMZN, ARM) moves more than 5% the session after its print, driven by AI-capex commentary rather than the headline EPS beat/miss.
forecasts.basis: Recent-quarter pattern reported in press coverage: AI spenders have been 'punished' even on in-line results while capex guidance drove the reaction (cited re: Alphabet's prior print). Pattern-based, not a hard data model.
forecasts.outcome: Multiple mega-cap reporters moved >5% on AI-capex commentary: MSFT +15.56%, META -8.0%, AMZN +15.46%, AAPL -7.19%, ARM -6.18%, QCOM -5.38%.
forecasts.lesson: The 'AI-capex commentary drives the reaction, not the EPS beat/miss' pattern held across nearly every reporter this week, not just one.

forecasts.forecast: US 10Y Treasury yield stays within 4.55-4.85% through Friday's close, i.e. does not break more than ~15bp outside Friday's 4.69% par level in either direction on a closing basis.
forecasts.basis: Friday's par curve (Treasury.gov) plus the week's binary catalysts (FOMC decision, GDP, ECI, 2Y/5Y/7Y auctions) that could move the long end; range width reflects the number of scheduled catalysts, not a statistical model.
forecasts.outcome: 10Y Treasury closed the week at 4.75% (Jul 31, Treasury.gov par curve) -- inside the 4.55-4.85% band despite a volatile week (FOMC, GDP, ECI, Iran escalation).
forecasts.lesson: Even a week stacked with binary catalysts kept the 10Y inside a ~30bp band; duration moved less than the equity-vol backdrop implied.

forecasts.forecast: Bitcoin trades in a $60,000-$72,000 range through Friday.
forecasts.basis: Spot $65,000 as of Sunday evening (CoinGecko), 24h change +0.9%; range sized at roughly ±10% around spot given no crypto-specific catalyst identified this week.
forecasts.outcome: Bitcoin traded within the $60,000-$72,000 band all week (high ~$64,914 Mon, low ~$62,944 Fri; $63,046 as of this run).
forecasts.lesson: Crypto stayed rangebound through a week of major equity and rates volatility -- no spillover catalyst materialized.

forecasts.forecast: The US-Iran ceasefire (in place since Apr 8, extended indefinitely Apr 21) holds through the week without a return to direct strikes, though talks on the Strait of Hormuz toll regime and reparations remain unresolved.
forecasts.basis: Press reports (AP/Times of Israel/Britannica '2026 Iran war' explainer) describe a two-day mutual pause as of Jul 26 with negotiations continuing; sourcing is Confirmed-multiple on the pause, but the underlying dispute (Hormuz tolls, reparations, ballistic-missile program) is unresolved, so probability is not higher.
forecasts.outcome: The US-Iran ceasefire did not hold: the US struck dozens of IRGC targets across Iran overnight Jul 29-30, and Iran retaliated against Jordan, Kuwait, and (reportedly) Egypt -- a direct return to strikes, not a continuation of the pause.
forecasts.lesson: This was the week's largest forecasting miss. A 'two-day mutual pause' with an unresolved underlying dispute (Hormuz tolls, reparations, missile program) should have been framed as fragile/reversible from the start, not assigned 60-70% odds of holding a full week. Track ceasefire-status forecasts with materially wider uncertainty bands and shorter horizons going forward.

forecasts.forecast: FOMC surprises with a 25bp rate hike on Jul 29 instead of a hold.
forecasts.basis: Press-reported CME FedWatch readings of a 35-39% hike probability as of Jul 23-25 (up from ~12% two weeks earlier, attributed to the Iran-driven oil spike), discounted downward for the weekend's oil-price reversal following the Jul 23-26 ceasefire pause, which is not yet reflected in the last-published FedWatch reads. Judgment adjustment, not a live model pull -- CME's FedWatch tool is outside this system's egress allowlist.
forecasts.outcome: FOMC held rather than hiking; the 20-30% hike probability did not materialize.
forecasts.lesson: The post-ceasefire-pause oil reversal (discounted into this forecast) correctly pointed toward a hold; the residual 20-30% was reasonable given the CME-reported hike odds at the time, but the ceasefire itself proved fragile days later, which this forecast could not have anticipated.

forecasts.forecast: Q2 2026 GDP advance estimate (Jul 30, 8:30 ET) prints in a 1.0-2.5% annualized range.
forecasts.basis: Atlanta Fed GDPNow tracking estimate of +1.7% annualized as of Jul 17 (fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDPNOW context via press reporting), widened both directions for typical tracking-estimate-to-actual error and the ten-day gap to the release. Supersedes the wider 1.5-3.0% band in forecast 2026-07-26-sun-2, which was made without GDPNow data.
forecasts.outcome: Q2 GDP printed +1.5%, squarely inside the GDPNow-informed 1.0-2.5% range.
forecasts.lesson: Anchoring to the actual GDPNow tracking estimate (rather than a generic default band) produced a better-centered forecast than the wider sun-2 range issued three days earlier without that data.

forecasts.forecast: Anubis posts leaked Fairlife (Coca-Cola) data to its leak site within 72 hours (by 2026-07-30), given today's extortion deadline passed without a confirmed payment or public resolution.
forecasts.basis: General pattern of ransomware groups following through on leak-site deadlines when no payment/settlement is publicly confirmed, weighed against the possibility of a quiet, unannounced settlement (common in corporate ransomware cases) or a further unannounced deadline extension. No group-specific follow-through-rate data was available this run.
forecasts.outcome: Anubis posted the leaked Fairlife (Coca-Cola) data to its leak site after the extortion deadline lapsed (surfaced 2026-07-28-pm).
forecasts.lesson: The base-rate pattern (ransomware groups following through absent a confirmed settlement) held in this case.

forecasts.forecast: NVDA does not close lower than today's -4.99% single-session move on any one day through Wednesday's (Jul 29) FOMC decision, absent on-the-record confirmation of the WSJ-reported $250B+ OpenAI financing figures.
forecasts.basis: Today's decline already re-priced the single-sourced report; absent a confirming or denying statement from Nvidia/OpenAI/SoftBank, no fresh catalyst is scheduled before Wednesday, and single-name moves of this size rarely repeat on consecutive sessions without new information. Range reflects genuine two-way uncertainty given Wednesday's Microsoft/Meta AI-capex earnings could pull sentiment either way intraday.
forecasts.outcome: NVDA closed +0.25% Jul 28 and -3.55%/-3.6% Jul 29 -- neither day closed lower (more negative) than Jul 27's -4.99% move, holding through Wednesday's FOMC.
forecasts.lesson: Single-name shock moves of this size did not repeat on consecutive sessions absent a fresh catalyst, consistent with the forecast's reasoning.

forecasts.forecast: Today's Nasdaq-focused chip-sector weakness (Nasdaq-100 futures -2.6% premarket) broadens into the US cash session, with XLK underperforming the broader S&P 500 by more than 1 percentage point at today's close.
forecasts.basis: Monday's cash session already showed contained, not broad, weakness from the original NVDA move (Dow and Russell held gains); today's move has a clearer cross-border catalyst chain via Samsung and SK Hynix's worst sessions in roughly two decades, but premarket futures moves regularly narrow by the cash open.
forecasts.outcome: XLK closed -1.84% on Jul 28 versus the S&P 500's +0.21-0.24%, a ~2.1 percentage-point underperformance -- exceeding the 1pp threshold.
forecasts.lesson: The cross-border Samsung/SK Hynix catalyst chain did broaden into the US cash session as flagged, not stay contained the way Monday's move had.

forecasts.forecast: Today's 7-Year Treasury Note auction ($44B, 1:00 PM ET) tails (weak demand) on FOMC-eve positioning.
forecasts.basis: Monday's 2-Year auction showed solid demand (2.66x cover, -0.5bp tail); the 7-Year is historically the most tail-prone tenor and this is the last coupon auction before Wednesday's FOMC decision, which can pull demand in either direction.
forecasts.outcome: The Jul 28 7-Year Note auction drew a 2.49x bid-to-cover -- described as average demand, not a tail.
forecasts.lesson: The most tail-prone tenor did not tail even immediately ahead of the FOMC decision; auction demand proved more resilient to event-risk positioning than the base rate implied.

forecasts.forecast: A Kyushu-based semiconductor or electronics manufacturer discloses facility damage or a production halt tied to the magnitude-7.1 Kumamoto earthquake within 48 hours.
forecasts.basis: No such disclosure as of this run; the region hosts meaningful chip/electronics manufacturing capacity, but M7-class quakes in this zone have historically caused more infrastructure than heavy-industry disruption.
forecasts.outcome: TSMC, Sony, and Tokyo Electron all disclosed Kumamoto-quake-related facility impacts (evacuations, a suspended fab) the same day, well inside the 48-hour window.
forecasts.lesson: The region's chip/electronics manufacturing footprint was large enough that a magnitude-7.1 quake did produce same-day disclosures, faster than the base rate for this quake class suggested.

forecasts.forecast: The FOMC hikes 25bp today rather than holding at 3.50-3.75%.
forecasts.basis: Pre-attack press-reported odds already ran as high as 38% hike probability (up from 10.7% a week earlier) on oil-driven inflation-expectations repricing; tonight's Iran attack and fresh ~3.5-3.6% oil jump is an additional hawkish input not yet reflected in any published odds reading as of this report's cutoff.
forecasts.outcome: The FOMC held rather than hiking, despite the fresh overnight Iran attack and oil jump cited as additional hawkish input.
forecasts.lesson: Even a same-day escalation (Iran's Jordan ballistic-missile attack) was not enough to tip a already-signaled hold into a hike -- the Fed's pre-meeting positioning proved more durable than the geopolitical shock.

forecasts.forecast: Iran carries out a further missile or drone attack, or the US takes explicit further military action beyond tonight's retaliatory strikes, within 48 hours of the Jordan base attack.
forecasts.basis: CENTCOM's own framing describes tonight's US-Saudi strikes as a proportionate response to a discrete attack, arguing against immediate further escalation; but Iran's shift from drone to ballistic-missile attacks is a real escalation in kind that argues for continued risk.
forecasts.outcome: The US struck dozens of IRGC targets across Iran overnight Jul 29-30 -- a major further US military action within 48 hours of the Jordan base attack, followed immediately by Iranian retaliation against Jordan, Kuwait, and Egypt.
forecasts.lesson: The shift from drone to ballistic-missile attacks correctly signaled continued escalation risk rather than a return to restraint.

forecasts.forecast: Iran carries out a further strike on a fourth country, or a confirmed high-casualty event occurs on either side, within 48 hours of tonight's US strike campaign on Iran.
forecasts.basis: Tonight's pattern already spans US strikes inside Iran plus Iranian retaliation against Jordan, Kuwait and reportedly Egypt in a single morning -- a broader footprint than any prior single exchange this report has tracked -- though CENTCOM's framing so far remains retaliatory/proportionate rather than an open-ended campaign.
forecasts.outcome: Iran struck Egypt (a fourth country beyond the existing Jordan/Kuwait/US-Iran pattern) the same night as the US strike campaign, confirmed by Egypt's own drone-strike acknowledgment -- resolving well inside the 48-hour window.
forecasts.lesson: This conflict's footprint kept broadening faster than a 'proportionate, contained response' framing implied; multi-country spillover within hours, not days, has now been the pattern twice.

forecasts.forecast: Q2 2026 GDP advance estimate (8:30 ET today) prints below the 1.0-2.5% annualized range from forecast 2026-07-27-am-2.
forecasts.basis: Atlanta Fed GDPNow at 1.54% (Jul 28) and prediction-market pricing (~88% probability of a print at or above 1.0%) both cluster around modest-but-positive growth within the existing forecast range; a below-range print would be a genuine surprise against that backdrop.
forecasts.outcome: Q2 GDP printed +1.5%, inside (not below) the existing 1.0-2.5% range.
forecasts.lesson: GDPNow's 1.54% tracking estimate and prediction-market pricing clustering near 'modest-but-positive' both correctly pointed away from a below-range surprise; the low 15-25% probability assigned here was well-calibrated.

forecasts.forecast: Apple or Amazon (or both) move more than 5% in the session following tonight's after-close earnings.
forecasts.basis: Three of the four mega-cap reporters this week (Microsoft, Meta, and to a lesser extent Arm/Qualcomm) have already moved more than 5% on results; Apple and Amazon face similar AI-capex-scrutiny dynamics, though Apple historically reacts more mutedly to earnings than these AI-infrastructure-exposed names.
forecasts.outcome: Both Apple (-7.19%) and Amazon (+15.46%) moved more than 5% in the session following their after-close earnings.
forecasts.lesson: As with the week's other mega-cap reporters, AI-capex/guidance scrutiny (Apple's weak guide, Amazon's AWS beat) drove outsized reactions on both sides.

forecasts.forecast: Microsoft retains at least half of today's 15.56% gain through Friday's close (i.e., does not close Friday more than ~8% below today's close).
forecasts.basis: Today's move reflects a confirmed Azure/capex beat plus a one-time $3.2B Anthropic-stake gain, not short covering alone, arguing for durability, though moves of this historic size have occasionally partially unwound on index-rebalancing or profit-taking flows in other names.
forecasts.outcome: Microsoft closed Jul 31 at $464.72, up a further +3.02% from Thursday's +15.51-15.56% close -- retaining the full gain and then some, not just half of it.
forecasts.lesson: A move backed by a confirmed Azure/capex beat plus a one-time equity-stake gain proved durable rather than mean-reverting, as the forecast's reasoning anticipated.

forecasts.forecast: No formal NATO Article 4 consultation is invoked over today's Poland missile-crash incident within 72 hours.
forecasts.basis: Poland's response so far (scrambling jets, government attribution statements without a confirmed Article 4 request as of this report's cutoff) has been measured; genuine uncertainty remains given this is described as a missile rather than debris, a more serious category of incursion.
forecasts.outcome: No NATO Article 4 consultation was invoked over the Poland missile-crash incident; NATO's Stoltenberg said no Article 4 until the investigation completed, and no formal consultation request followed in the days after.
forecasts.lesson: A 'no formal escalation' forecast held even though the incident (a Russian missile crashing on NATO territory) was serious; alliance-level formal mechanisms have a higher activation bar than the underlying event severity alone would suggest.

forecasts.forecast: Iran's claim of destroying/damaging six F-35s and killing personnel in a drone strike on Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base, Kuwait, is not independently confirmed by CENTCOM or the Kuwaiti government within 48 hours.
forecasts.basis: This conflict's prior pattern of Iranian/IRGC-sourced damage and casualty claims going unconfirmed by Western governments for days or being quietly revised; weighed against the unusually large and specific scale of this particular claim, which would ordinarily draw a faster US response either way.
forecasts.outcome: Iran's claim of destroying/damaging six F-35s at Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base, Kuwait was never confirmed by CENTCOM or the Kuwaiti government; CENTCOM's public position ('No US aircraft were destroyed or damaged') stands unchanged a week later.
forecasts.lesson: IRGC-sourced damage/casualty claims in this conflict continued their established pattern of going unconfirmed by Western governments, even for claims specific and large enough (six F-35s) to ordinarily invite a rebuttal.

forecasts.forecast: Employment Cost Index Q2 2026 (8:30 ET today) prints at or below approximately 0.5% quarter-over-quarter, continuing the wage-growth deceleration seen in Q1's 3.4% year-over-year reading.
forecasts.basis: Trading Economics' model-based estimate of ~0.40% Q/Q is the only forward figure available this run (not a polled Street consensus); genuine two-way uncertainty given no live consensus data was reachable.
forecasts.outcome: Employment Cost Index printed +0.9% Q/Q, well above the ~0.5% ceiling and roughly double the ~0.40% Trading Economics model estimate.
forecasts.lesson: The only available forward figure (a model-based estimate, not a polled Street consensus) undershot badly; this is the second consecutive week a wage/cost print ran hotter than the available estimate, worth flagging as a pattern to watch.

forecasts.forecast: The S&P 500 closes higher today, extending Thursday's rally.
forecasts.basis: Premarket futures point higher (ES +0.5%) after both Amazon and Apple beat estimates after Thursday's close, but today's Employment Cost Index release and the unconfirmed Iran-Kuwait strike claim are each independent sources of intraday reversal risk not yet reflected in the premarket tape.
forecasts.outcome: The S&P 500 closed Jul 31 at 7,504.53, up +0.90%, extending Thursday's rally as forecast.
forecasts.lesson: Premarket futures direction (ES +0.5% on the Amazon/Apple beats) held through the full session despite the hot ECI print and unconfirmed Iran-Kuwait strike claim, both flagged as reversal risks that did not materialize.

forecasts.forecast: Novo Nordisk (NVO) does not recover half of today's ~8.6% decline within the next 5 trading sessions (closes below approximately $49.90 through Aug 7).
forecasts.basis: A failed pivotal cardiovascular trial removes a major pipeline asset — a fundamental repricing that historically proves more durable than a sentiment-driven earnings-reaction selloff.
forecasts.outcome: Novo Nordisk closed the Aug 7 session at $47.24, well below the ~$49.90 half-recovery threshold, after three consecutive sell-side downgrades (HSBC, Wall Street Zen, UBS) through the week.
forecasts.lesson: A failed pivotal trial repriced NVO more durably than a sentiment-driven earnings selloff would have; the stock never mounted a meaningful recovery attempt all week.

forecasts.forecast: The Gaza disarmament roadmap required within 14 days of Thursday's Board of Peace announcement (due on or around Aug 13) is not finalized on schedule.
forecasts.basis: Coverage gathered this run notes both Israeli skepticism that Hamas will actually disarm and a senior Hamas official's comments suggesting the disarmament/withdrawal sequencing is still contested — a genuinely two-way outcome given both sides have nonetheless publicly engaged with the process.

forecasts.forecast: Coinbase (COIN) draws at least one sell-side price-target cut within 5 trading days of today's Q2 report (third consecutive quarterly loss, revenue -14% YoY).
forecasts.basis: Pattern of analyst reaction to consecutive-quarter deterioration in a widely covered name, weighed against a broader crypto-sector narrative that could offset company-specific concern.
forecasts.outcome: Coinbase drew multiple sell-side price-target cuts within the window: Mizuho (Jul 31, to $155), Cantor Fitzgerald (Aug 3, to $184), and Citigroup (to $210), following the third consecutive quarterly loss.
forecasts.lesson: The base-rate pattern (analyst cuts following consecutive-quarter deterioration in a widely covered name) held cleanly, with cuts arriving from multiple firms rather than just one.

forecasts.forecast: WTI crude (front-month) does not close Monday Aug 3's session more than 5% away from Friday Jul 31's $84.67 reference close in either direction.
forecasts.basis: The Iran de-escalation news Trump announced Saturday night is explicitly disputed by Iran itself, arguing against markets committing to a clean, large one-directional move on Monday's open; futures/commodities had not yet reopened for the week at this report's generation time so no live pricing signal was available to anchor this forecast.
forecasts.outcome: WTI closed Monday Aug 3 at $80.34, a -5.11% move from Friday Jul 31's $84.67 reference close -- just outside the +/-5% band (the 5%-down threshold was $80.44).
forecasts.lesson: A razor-thin miss (about $0.10, roughly 0.1 percentage point outside the band): the disputed Iran de-escalation narrative drove oil's Monday reaction slightly harder than the forecast's two-way-uncertainty framing anticipated.

forecasts.forecast: The paused US/Israel strikes on Iran resume, or a materially escalatory event (a further tanker attack, a confirmed Iranian rejection of deal terms, a new US/Israeli strike) occurs within the week.
forecasts.basis: Iran has publicly denied Trump's account that it requested a pause and agreed to deal terms; the underlying escalation drivers (Hormuz tanker attacks, suspected Iran-linked US cyberattacks) both occurred in the days immediately before the announcement and have not visibly stopped.
forecasts.outcome: The underlying escalation drivers did not stop: a further Strait of Hormuz tanker attack (Velos Amber) was confirmed within the week, satisfying the forecast's 'further tanker attack' trigger, even though US/Israel strikes did not resume.
forecasts.lesson: Framing the forecast around multiple alternative triggers (strikes OR a tanker attack OR a rejection of terms) correctly captured that this conflict de-escalated on the diplomatic/military track while continuing on the maritime-harassment track.

forecasts.forecast: A third tanker or commercial vessel is hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz this week.
forecasts.basis: Two incidents involving the same shipping manager's LNG carriers occurred within the past week alone (Gaslog Salem at Damietta, Gaslog Shanghai in the Strait), with no claim of responsibility or resolution for either.
forecasts.outcome: A third Hormuz-area vessel (Velos Amber) was struck within the week, confirmed by Aug 4 reporting -- the third incident in the tracked pattern (Gaslog Salem, Gaslog Shanghai, Velos Amber).
forecasts.lesson: The accelerating-incident-pace base rate (roughly one every 2-3 days) correctly anticipated continuation before any de-escalation signal on this specific risk channel had materialized.

forecasts.forecast: SpaceX (SPCX) moves more than 8% in the session following Tuesday Aug 4's first-ever public earnings report.
forecasts.basis: SPCX has traded with high realized volatility since its June 2026 IPO, and this is its first quarterly disclosure as a public company with no prior print to anchor investor expectations.
forecasts.outcome: SpaceX closed the Aug 5 session (the day after its first-ever public earnings) at $108.27, down 13.62% from the Aug 4 close of $125.33 -- well past the 8% threshold.
forecasts.lesson: A binary first-print catalyst with no prior quarter to anchor expectations produced an outsized move, as elevated short interest and a wide sell-side estimate range both signaled going in.

forecasts.forecast: A new US state or a critical (non-water) infrastructure sector discloses a cyberattack related to the suspected Iran-linked water-utility intrusion campaign this week.
forecasts.basis: The campaign has already spread from Minnesota to Michigan and reportedly touched at least seven states in total per federal officials, though FBI attribution to Iran remains preliminary and unconfirmed.
forecasts.outcome: The water-utility cyberattack campaign expanded to include Georgia, South Dakota, and New Jersey as newly disclosed states within the week, beyond the seven states known as of Aug 2.
forecasts.lesson: A campaign already showing a consistent weekly-expansion pattern continued that pattern; the FBI/press-sourced attribution to Iran remained preliminary throughout, as flagged.

forecasts.forecast: Base scenario: Iran pause holds without confirmation either way; jobs report roughly in line with recent trend; SpaceX earnings/lockup pass without a broad-market spillover -- choppy, mixed week with single-name volatility exceeding index-level volatility.
forecasts.basis: Analytic judgment weighing the disputed-but-not-yet-reversed de-escalation, a two-way jobs-report risk, and a structurally volatile but idiosyncratic SpaceX catalyst -- not a statistical model output.
forecasts.outcome: Choppy, single-name-volatility-dominated week and no broad-market SpaceX-lockup spillover both held as forecast, but the jobs report was not 'roughly in line with recent trend' -- it was a shock miss (-23,000 vs +83K-97.5K estimates), the week's most consequential single surprise.
forecasts.lesson: The 'choppy, mixed week' framing was directionally right, but naming the jobs report as an in-line, low-drama input understated its actual role as the week's dominant catalyst -- a reminder that a Critical-tier release deserves wider two-way framing even when no forward consensus signal is available.

forecasts.forecast: Bull scenario: Iran deal firms up with some form of mutual confirmation; jobs report shows continued gradual cooling read as Fed-friendly; SpaceX earnings beat -- oil lower, risk-on tone, yields ease modestly.
forecasts.basis: Requires multiple favorable confirmations (Iranian statement, jobs data, earnings) to align; analytic judgment, not a statistical model.
forecasts.outcome: Several bull-case elements matched (oil closed the week lower, WTI -2.69%; equities were risk-on with the S&P at a fresh record; the 10Y yield eased from 4.75% to 4.65%; the Iran-Oman corridor deal did firm up with mutual confirmation), but the jobs report showed a shock deterioration rather than 'continued gradual cooling,' and SpaceX's earnings were mixed (revenue beat, but a $60B acquisition disclosure and heavy capex triggered an initial selloff) rather than a clean beat.
forecasts.lesson: This scenario's market-outcome predictions (oil lower, risk-on, yields easing) proved more durable than its causal story (a benign, gradual jobs cooling) -- the market ended up in a bull-scenario place via a bear-scenario datapoint (a weak jobs report read as rate-cut-friendly), a distinction worth separating in future scenario writing.

forecasts.forecast: Bear scenario: Iran continues denying the deal publicly without escalating; a weak jobs report reads as labor-market cracking rather than gradual cooling; SpaceX lockup pressures the stock mechanically -- yields fall on growth fear, SPCX-led space-sector weakness.
forecasts.basis: Analytic judgment; a soft-but-not-shock combination of the week's known catalysts.
forecasts.outcome: The jobs report did read as labor-market cracking rather than gradual cooling, as this scenario anticipated, but Iran did not continue denying the deal (it progressed to a mutually confirmed Hormuz corridor agreement), the SpaceX lockup did not pressure the stock mechanically (SPCX rose 6.14% through the lockup session), and space-sector weakness did not materialize -- the sector posted its strongest week of the cycle (VOYG +49%, RDW +41%, PLTR +37% weekly).
forecasts.lesson: The single correctly-anticipated element (a weak jobs report) was outweighed by three inverted calls; bear scenarios built around multiple simultaneous negative catalysts are vulnerable when even one pillar (here, the SpaceX lockup) breaks the other way, since markets don't average scenario legs -- they follow whichever catalyst dominates.

forecasts.forecast: Shock scenario: strikes resume, a further tanker is hit with casualties, or the suspected Iran-linked cyberattacks are confirmed to have caused an operational water-safety incident -- oil spike, broad risk-off, safe-haven bid, VIX back above its recent range.
forecasts.basis: Requires a confirmed, severe escalation beyond anything observed as of this report's cutoff; analytic judgment, not a statistical model.
forecasts.outcome: None of the shock triggers occurred: no strikes resumed, no tanker attack caused casualties, and no water-utility cyberattack was confirmed to have caused an operational safety incident. Oil fell rather than spiked, equities closed at records rather than risk-off, and VIX ended the week at 14.90 -- below its recent range, not above it.
forecasts.lesson: Assigning only 10-15% to the shock scenario was well-calibrated; the week's actual tail risk (a jobs-report shock) came from a completely different vector than the scenario matrix's geopolitical/cyber shock triggers, a reminder that scenario matrices built around the week's most visible risk (Iran) can miss the actual surprise.

forecasts.forecast: This morning's premarket equity rally and oil selloff (tied to Trump's disputed Iran de-escalation announcement) partially or fully reverses intraday, because no US-Iran talks occur today or Iran issues a further, more forceful denial.
forecasts.basis: Iran's government has denied the deal at multiple levels (Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Fars, Mehr, and the acting Defense Minister) this weekend, a broader denial than last week's state-media-only pushback; genuine two-way uncertainty given FM Araghchi's narrower Iran-Oman Hormuz-management claim is not itself disputed and could still anchor some form of de-escalation.
forecasts.outcome: Monday's premarket rally and oil selloff extended into the cash session rather than reversing: the S&P 500 closed +1.48% and the Nasdaq +2.13%, both holding (and building on) the premarket gains despite Iran's continued denial of any deal.
forecasts.lesson: A harder, multi-source Iranian denial was not sufficient on its own to reverse a move once the cash session got underway -- price action, once established, proved more durable than the fragility of its underlying geopolitical premise.

forecasts.forecast: Todd Blanche's AG nomination advances out of the Senate Judiciary Committee at Tuesday's 9:00 AM ET vote.
forecasts.basis: Both previously-holdout Republicans (Cornyn and Tillis) issued a joint statement Monday backing the vote, after the disputed anti-weaponization fund was rescinded; probability is not higher only because no vote has actually occurred yet and last-minute reversals have happened elsewhere in this same nomination fight.
forecasts.outcome: The Senate Judiciary Committee voted 12-10 to advance Todd Blanche's nomination at Tuesday's session, as both previously-holdout Republicans (Cornyn and Tillis) followed through on their stated support.
forecasts.lesson: Public, on-record commitments from the deciding votes ahead of a scheduled committee session were a reliable signal here, consistent with this forecast's high (80-90%) confidence.

forecasts.forecast: Today's equity rally (S&P +1.48%) holds through Wednesday's close -- the S&P 500 does not close below Friday Jul 31's 7,489.72 level at any point through Wednesday Aug 5.
forecasts.basis: Today's session showed the market absorbing a harder Iranian denial without reversing, and tomorrow's earnings (SpaceX) and JOLTS data are the more likely near-term swing factors; genuine two-way uncertainty remains given the underlying Iran dispute is unresolved and could still produce a fresh shock.
forecasts.outcome: The S&P 500 closed above Friday Jul 31's 7,489.72 level every session through Wednesday Aug 5 (Aug 3: 7,600.50; Aug 4: 7,736.52; Aug 5: 7,723.55), holding the rally without a single close-below breach.
forecasts.lesson: Absent a fresh shock, a rally built on a hardening (not softening) risk backdrop -- Iran's continued denial did not reverse the market's read -- proved durable through the mid-week SpaceX/JOLTS catalysts.

forecasts.forecast: The Ceuta migrant-crossing death toll is reconciled to a single widely-cited figure (rather than the current 67-88 range across outlets) within one week.

forecasts.forecast: Todd Blanche's Attorney General nomination fails on the Senate floor (either Murkowski or Cassidy votes no, or an additional GOP senator defects).
forecasts.basis: Sen. Collins's Aug 4 no-vote announcement leaves exactly two GOP senators (Murkowski, Cassidy) uncommitted with distinct, unresolved concerns and only one allowable additional defection given the 53-47 majority; no public whip count was found confirming either senator's final position.
forecasts.outcome: Todd Blanche's nomination did not fail: Sen. Murkowski did vote no (alongside Collins, already committed), but Sen. Cassidy's yes vote alone was sufficient to reach exactly 50 Republican votes, and the nomination was confirmed 50-49 in the early hours of Saturday, Aug 8.
forecasts.lesson: A single additional defection (Murkowski) was not enough to sink the nomination once Cassidy's support held -- the forecast correctly identified Murkowski and Cassidy as the pivotal votes but underweighted how little margin for error a 53-47 majority actually needs when only one senator (Collins) was a certain no.

forecasts.forecast: A fifth Strait of Hormuz-area vessel incident is reported before today's Closing Brief (16:30 ET cutoff).
forecasts.basis: Four incidents in roughly a week (Gaslog Salem, Gaslog Shanghai, Velos Amber, Minoan Pioneer) is an accelerating pace; UKMTO/Bloomberg describe Hormuz shipping traffic as 'at a trickle.' forecasts.forecast: SpaceX (SPCX) moves more than +/-5% on Aug 6, the day of its ~$116B share-lockup expiration, extending or reversing today's -13.6% close.

Genuine two-way uncertainty given both dynamics are plausible.
forecasts.outcome: SpaceX closed the Aug 6 lockup-expiration session at $114.92, up 6.14% from Aug 5's $108.27 close -- exceeding the +/-5% threshold in the 'extends/reverses' direction of stabilization rather than further mechanical selling.
forecasts.lesson: The 'sell the news' stabilization dynamic (float increase already priced in ahead of the lockup) dominated over mechanical selling pressure -- a useful data point for framing future lockup-expiration forecasts in this name.

forecasts.forecast: Todd Blanche is confirmed as Attorney General in Saturday's (Aug 8) scheduled final Senate vote (i.e. neither Murkowski nor Cassidy votes no, or only one does and no other GOP senator defects).
forecasts.basis: Two senators uncommitted with distinct concerns (Murkowski on the rescinded fund, Cassidy on White House independence); no public no-commitment from either as of this report; historical base rate favors confirmation once a floor vote is scheduled by leadership.
forecasts.outcome: Todd Blanche was confirmed 50-49 in Saturday's early-morning vote; exactly one of the two tracked uncommitted senators (Murkowski) voted no, with Cassidy voting yes and no additional GOP senator defecting beyond the already-known Collins no vote.
forecasts.lesson: The historical base rate favoring confirmation once a floor vote is scheduled by leadership held, even with two senators publicly uncommitted through the final days -- the margin (50-49) shows this was a genuinely close call the base rate happened to resolve correctly.

forecasts.forecast: Iran and Oman announce a Hormuz shipping-corridor joint statement or deal by end-of-day Friday, Aug 7.
forecasts.basis: An unnamed Gulf official cited 50-50 odds to CNN; Trump's 'a lot of progress' framing and the absence of any new Hormuz incident this run weigh slightly positive, offset by Iran's continued formal denial of direct US talks and the deputy FM's caution that any deal would not automatically reopen the strait.

forecasts.lesson: The 50-50-odds framing from an unnamed Gulf official proved too pessimistic; once coordinates were reported 'finalized' (per Wednesday's am edition), the remaining step to a public joint announcement moved faster than the repeated near-miss pattern this report had tracked through the week.

forecasts.forecast: Tomorrow's session sees at least half of today's ten broadly-weak financials/alternative-asset-manager names (JPM, BAC, C, WFC, GS, MS, IBKR, HOOD, COIN, KKR, BX, APO, ARES) close lower again, indicating the move was not a one-day event.
